text.text: Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr. will miss El Clasico against FC Barcelona on Oct. 25 after being suspended for four games for the red card he received in Real Madrid's last home game, against Villarreal at the Bernabeu. The Brazilian forward came on in the 52nd minute and was sent off 20 minutes later. Vinicius Jr. thought he had scored, and Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho celebrated alongside his team and ran over to him a few seconds before VAR ruled out the goal and sent him off. The VAR check showed Vinicius Jr. had pulled Nathan Saliba's hair before scoring. The Spanish Football Federation's rules state that pulling an opponent's hair is violent conduct, and Vinicius was suspended for the upcoming four Real Madrid matches against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander and Valencia. The federation's competition committee gave Vinicius a two-game ban for "violent conduct, without the possibility of playing the ball" and two additional games "for arguing with the referee with an aggressive attitude and having to be restrained by his teammates." text.text: SMRITI Mandhana has captained India before. The job, and the responsibility in itself, is not new to her. But when the 29-year-old walks out on the field in Raipur during the first T20I against Zimbabwe, it will mark a new beginning. Not just for Mandhana the captain, but also in Indian women's cricket.Captaincy change in the women's team does not happen so often. At least not since 2012. From having six captains between 2000 and 2012, India went on to have only two skippers over the last 14 years — Mithali Raj and Harmanpreet Kaur.Raj led India in ODIs and Tests till her retirement in 2022 while Kaur, who took over in the shortest format in 2016, inherited the full-time job four years ago. Though Kaur led India to historic ODI WC triumph, the time had come for transition. Now, the baton has been passed on to Mandhana — the 29-year-old who has already built a legendary career — following two back-to-back early exits in T20 World Cups.Mandhana, on Friday, will lead India for the first time as a full-time skipper in Raipur. text.text: Djokovic’s China Open title last week marked the first of his season, and it lifted him three places to No. 8 in the official rankings. This put him into the last qualifying spot for the Race to Turin, but a first-match loss at the Shanghai Masters has since put his end-of-season hopes in jeopardy. Novak Djokovic defeated Alex de Minaur in the China Open final last Tuesday, when de Minaur retired with a groin injury while trailing 7-6(3), 0-1. The win was the Serbian’s seventh Beijing title and the 102nd of his career, now placing him just one behind Roger Federer. It was also his first ATP title since Athens last November, and it couldn’t have come at a better time. Djokovic extended his impressive unbeaten record at the tournament to 34-0 with the title. En route to the final, he beat top seed Alexander Zverev in the quarterfinals and advanced to the final when Daniil Medvedev was defaulted from their semifinal match. The victory ended a rough stretch for Djokovic this season, where he lost in the first round of the US Open and had gone the whole year without a title. text.text: Max Verstappen will share a track with Valentino Rossi for the first time in a competitive setting this weekend, with the pair set to go wheel-to-wheel at the GT World Challenge Endurance finale in Portimão. Verstappen lines up in a Mercedes AMG GT3 EVO, while Rossi will be behind the wheel of a BMW M4 GT3 EVO. The four-time F1 drivers' champion has already made clear he would rather not run into the MotoGP legend out on circuit. But is there really anything for Verstappen to worry about? Few people are better placed to answer that than Kelvin van der Linde. The South African BMW factory driver spent a lengthy spell as Rossi's team-mate and has shared a car with the Italian on several occasions, giving him a unique insight into how the nine-time MotoGP champion has adapted to four wheels. Speaking to RacingNews365 earlier this year, Van der Linde gave a frank assessment of where Rossi stands as a GT racer. "It's a tricky question," he says. "I think that success in MotoGP came because he just had an incredible talent for two wheels. "He was in the prime of his career back then. He was the perfect age at that time. It comes ahead of Hart becoming Verstappen's new full-time race engineer from 2027 as Lambiase prepares to complete his move to McLaren. Lambiase, who has served as Verstappen's race engineer since 2016, announced earlier this year that he will join McLaren as chief racing officer in due course. McLaren commented at the time that Lambiase will start work at Woking 'no later' than 2028. The 2026 season will therefore mark Lambiase's last year as Verstappen's race engineer as he prepares to make the move to his new team. As reported by PlanetF1.com at the time , it emerged in July that Hart will take over from Lambiase on a full-time basis from 2027. text.text: Kristaps Porzingis is back with the Golden State Warriors , but when he'll be back playing in an NBA game remains a mystery. The Warriors confirmed in a statement that Porzingis returned to the team's practice facility on Tuesday, Oct. 13, and remains out indefinitely after he missed all of the team's training camp and preseason games. Officials offered no indication on when Porzingis might return to practice or resume on-court activities. The 31-year-old center has battled injuries throughout his NBA career. His latest issues have proven especially concerning because doctors have yet to identify a long-term solution that would allow him to return to full basketball activities. But the 7-foot-2 center took to social media to reassure fans in conjunction with the Warriors' announcement on Wednesday, dismissing online speculation about his health and insisting he's "getting better and better." "I appreciate all the internet doctors trying to diagnose and help, but I'm in the best hands. So everyone can relax now ... and I don’t have hiv or aids," Porzingis wrote on X. text.text: Rafael Jodar’s latest win at the Shanghai Masters has been overshadowed by an incident in the second set that led to a code violation. Jodar moved into the quarter-finals with a 6-7(4), 6-4, 6-2 win over Botic van de Zandschulp. He is only the second player to reach the last eight in Shanghai before their 21st birthday, after Jakub Mensik. Overall, it is the fourth time this year the Spaniard has reached the last eight of a Masters 1000 event. An achievement that has only been matched or beaten by Arthur Fils, Jannik Sinner and Alexander Zverev. At the start of the second set, Jodar was heard shouting to the ball kid in Spanish, ‘Dame la puta toalla, coño!’ which translates to ‘Give me the bloody towel, for fuck’s sake!’ The remarks were picked up by the Spanish-speaking umpire Jimmy Pinoargote, who swiftly issued a warning to the tennis star before an argument between the two started. “ He’s not listening to me, mate, I’m talking to him… And I haven’t said anything wrong. Good grief!” Newspaper El Pais quoted Jodar as saying . “Rafa, ask me to sort it out and I’ll ask him, but not like that, ” Pinoargote responded. “That’s not how we talk to them [the ball boys]…” He later added.

report.text: On a night dominated by the apparent status of Kristaps Porzingis, the absence of the Latvian big was felt at times during the Golden State Warriors’ 101-89 win over the Los Angeles Lakers at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada. Steve Kerr’s intention to spread the floor in a so-called ‘5-out’ alignment banked on players who are able to space to floor — including their center. Porzingis happens to fit that profile, while also being 7-foot-3-inches. Without Porzingis — and also not having Al Horford available tonight — the Warriors were not only small, they were bereft of shooting and spacing personnel. That was apparent at times during this game, where the Warriors were able to rally back from a significant deficit, albeit during a time when both teams’ main characters’ nights were finished (one of them, Luka Doncic, did not suit up for the Lakers). Once again, it was rookie Yaxel Lendeborg who stood out. He finished with 17 points, 5 rebounds, and 4 assists in just under 24 minutes of time on the floor.
